messages:
Sam: heads up — acme-prod reports a sharp p99 spike in eu-west-1 starting ~08:15 UTC. Customer says realtime responses ~>10s intermittently, p95 around 1.2s. Sample req_ids: req_0a12, req_0a15. Seen 503s in some traces. Could be admission/worker pileup. cc @Marco @Priya
Priya: thanks — do we have any traces or the request examples? any tenant-level concurrency changes?
Sam: attaching quick repro curl we got from them and a tiny log snippet:

Sam: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"short prompt","request_id":"req_0a12"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?tenant=acme-prod
```

Sam: logs -> "admission: enqueueing request tenant=acme-prod; inflight=23; limit=20" and repeated "admission: rejecting request tenant=acme-prod code=overloaded"

Marco: sounds like tenant cap hit + backlog. can someone run these two queries in graphite/prometheus: 

Marco: ```promql
sum(inflight_requests{tenant="acme-prod"}) by (zone)
rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="acme-prod"}[5m])
histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m]))
```

Marco: also check worker saturation: `kubectl top pods -n inference --selector=tenant=acme-prod` and `kubectl get pods -n inference -l tenant=acme-prod -o wide`
Priya: got it — Sam can you paste the trace id(s) for the 503s? need to pull full trace to see if it's waiting in admit queue vs kernel time.
Sam: trace ids: trace:abcd1234, trace:abcd1235. Pulling now. Also customer said they started a big send at 08:12 (burst from their side).

Liz: if this is tenant-level fairshare, customer spike would push them over their concurrency limit and cause queued requests. short-term mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase tenant concurrency cap (eg 20->40), 2) enable request-priority for realtime routes, 3) route non-critical traffic to queued/batch path. Which is fastest?
Marco: fastest is to bump the tenant cap for acme-prod. risk: higher tail on infra if they keep sending; but we can also add a soft token-bucket to smooth. If we patch cap, do canary to a single zone first.
Sam: customer OK with temporary bump while we triage. requesting approval to patch config now.
Marco: i approve a controlled bump + 10m canary. use infra runbook step: `infractl tenants update --id acme-prod --concurrency 40 --apply --reason "p99 surge 1746054321"` and watch inflight and p99.
Sam: running now. will post rollout id.
DeployBot: rollout started: run_id=rb-20240628-77, target=acme-prod, change="concurrency 20->40", mode=canary(zone=eu-west-1a) :rocket:
Priya: when bump goes in, please capture new prometheus series + traces for the same req_ids so we can compare waiting time vs service time.
Sam: rollout applied to eu-west-1a canary. seeing inflight jump then steady. immediate p99 dropped from ~10.8s -> 1.15s over last 2m. continuing to monitor.
Marco: nice. next steps: 1) collect full traces for trace abcd1234/5 and confirm time spent in admit queue vs model execution, 2) run back-pressure sim in staging to reproduce behavior and tune default tenant caps, 3) add alert that fires when tenant inflight > 0.9*cap for >1m.
Liz: I'll notify CS and update the incident ticket with mitigation + ask customer to throttle burst while we schedule long-term change (rate-limiter smoothing).
Sam: customer confirms improved UX. tagging this thread for postmortem if traces show systemic issue. :thumbsup:
DeployBot: rollout rb-20240628-77 completed to remaining zones (eu-west-1b,c) — status=success.
Marco: thanks all. capturing runbook notes in infra-runbooks/tenant-cap-adjust.md and scheduling a small follow-up to set better defaults and autoscaling guards.
Sam: closing thread once we have the trace analysis attached to the ticket.
